correctness.rationale: Semigroup powers exactly match iterates of the swap-equivariant transformation. Stationarity plus commutativity forces all cycles to be diagonal fixed points, equivalent to two weighted rooted forests. The diagonal minor has determinant r n^(n-r-1); the off-diagonal-orbit minor has determinant n(n+2m)^(m-1), with m=n(n-1)/2, including r=n boundary. Product gives binom(n,r)r n^(n^2-r-2); the exact binomial conditional law and Poisson limit follow by normalization. A sharp maximum depth follows from the quotient-forest height. Two independently implemented finite predicates agree across all n=2 and n=3 binary operations, verifying coefficients, not replacing the proof.

value.rationale: The count concerns semigroup-power dynamics of all binary operations, a natural invariant unaddressed by the inspected recent classifications of ideals/idempotents. It completely resolves the limiting-rank distribution at every n, shows exact n^-2 probability of stationary constant powers, an asymptotic e/n² rarity law, a conditional Poisson limit, and a sharp stabilized-depth extremal bound. The classical forest matrix-tree tool does not trivialize the essential swap-equivariant reduction and orientation multiplicities; this is neither a selected small-n census nor a renamed idempotency statement.
